influences.name: The Beatles
influences.context: Born in 1952, Karlheinz Bartos (Kraftwerk shortened his name to save money on lettering) was turned onto music the moment he heard the opening chord of The Beatles' A Hard Day's Night as a 12-year-old.

influences.name: Can
influences.context: Later he played in bands, took acid while listening to Can and pursued a career as a classical percussionist

influences.name: Claudio Monteverdi
influences.context: When I started in Kraftwerk, one of my typical days looked like this: in the morning we listened to and discussed Claudio Monteverdi's 1607 opera L'Orfeo in music history

influences.name: Benjamin Britten
influences.context: Ear training and piano lessons followed. Then we would perhaps rehearse a few bars on the vibraphone for a concert of new music over the weekend, and in the evening we'd go to the Opera House for a performance of Benjamin Britten's 1973 score for Death In Venice.

influences.name: Karlheinz Stockhausen
influences.context: The next day I was rehearsing music from Karlheinz Stockhausen.

influences.name: Stravinsky
influences.context: At that time, Stravinsky's Sacre Du Printemps was on the repertoire of the Deutsche Oper Am Rhein.

influences.name: Bob Dylan
influences.context: You can't get rid of Bob Dylan and The Beatles and the black music from America, and all the music from London, as it's all too close.

influences.name: Richard Wright
influences.context: From my point of view, Richard Wright's setup and his way of playing the keyboard was a great template for my former partner.

influences.name: Ray Manzarek
influences.context: Ray Manzarek was also an important figure.

influences.name: Brian Bennett
influences.context: Cliff had a really good band, The Shadows, and a good drummer, Brian Bennett. He did the intro to this wonderful song called Do You Want To Dance?, originally a Bobby Freeman song. So my subconscious brain from when I was a kid transferred this sequence by an English drummer into the song Numbers

influences.name: Elvis Presley
influences.context: When I was growing up, I was listening to the songs my sister was playing on her stereo player. She was in love with Elvis Presley and Cliff Richard too for some reason

influences.name: Cliff Richard
influences.context: She was in love with Elvis Presley and Cliff Richard too for some reason

influences.name: Jaki Liebezeit
influences.context: One of my favourite drummers is Jaki Liebezeit from Can, just a total, monstrous clockwork machine.

influences.name: Kraftwerk
influences.context: Yeah, but only in the later phase of their career. When I was 13 they played at a rave called Tribal Gathering. They were just this myth really and I remember begging my mum to let me go. I heard the live set on the radio. At the time I was already into Electronic music - I had a drum machine and synths - but the sound they were creating was kind of otherworldly, yet incredibly mechanical and human.
